entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard on the question of admission.
The present appeal appears arguable, hence admitted for final hearing.

Heard on IA No.16283 of 2024, first application under Section 389 (1) of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (herein after referred to as the Code) = Section 430 (1) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) for suspension of remaining jail sentence and grant of bail on behalf of appellant - Munna Maharaj @ Sarvan S/o Shri Salakram Sharma .

Vide judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 29.07.2024 passed in Sessions Trial No.28 of 2022 by learned Second Additional Sessions Judge, Ganjbasauda, District Vidisha (MP), the present appellant stands convicted under Section 376 (1) of Indian Penal Code, 1860 and has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a term of ten years with fine of Rs.2,000/- with usual default stipulation.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is aged about sixty five years and has been falsely implicated in the case.
The judgment is full of conjectures and surmises; and serious infirmities in the prosecution case has been ignored.
He further submits that in statement 2 CRA-9154-2024 under Section 164 of the Code, the victim has not mentioned anything about the alleged incident and the whole case is based on a concocted story.

At the time of incident, allegedly fifty persons were present and in such a situation, such type of incident was not possible and for this learned counsel appearing for the appellant has referred to statement of Dr. Rambabu Meena (PW-6) and also Dr. Shikha Raghuwanshi (PW-11) along with paragraph No.11 of the impugned judgment.
He submits that the appellant is suffering incarceration since nine months.
The appeal being of the year 2024 is not likely to be heard finally in near future.
There is a strong case in favour of the appellant and has fair chance of success.

Hence, under such circumstances, a prayer is made Munna Maharaj Baba@Sarwan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132843750/
1 for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail.

entities.text: Munna Maharaj Baba@Sarwan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent - State has opposed the prayer referring to DNA Report, which has been found positive and also paragraph No.15 of statement of the prosecutrix (PW-1).

Learned counsel further submits that ample evidence is available on record to connect the appellant with the alleged crime and evidence available on record has been properly appreciated by the learned trial Court, therefore, no exception can be taken to the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence, therefore, prays for dismissal of suspension application, as it sans merit.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
In the aforesaid factual backdrop and looking to the evidence in entirety, this Court is not inclined to grant suspension of remaining custodial 3 CRA-9154-2024 sentence of the appellant.
Accordingly, IA No.16283 of 2024 is dismissed.

Pending IA No.21845 of 2024 , IA No.1467 of 2025 ,
IA No.4547 of 2025 and IA No.5211 of 2025 , applications for urgent hearing also stand disposed off.
Let the matter be listed for final hearing in due course.
In the meantime, let the record be requisitioned, if not already received.

(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE Adnan Munna Maharaj Baba@Sarwan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132843750/
2
